about: Bruno Giacosa was one of the defining figures of Barbaresco and Barolo. Born in 1929 into a family of wine merchants in Neive, he was the third generation after his grandfather Carlo and father Mario, and left school during the Second World War to work in the business at fifteen. For decades he made wine from grapes bought from growers whose vineyards he knew row by row, later adding estate vineyards under the Falletto name. Since his death in 2018 the house has been led by his daughter Bruna Giacosa.

This Nebbiolo d’Alba comes from the Roero, on the left bank of the Tanaro across from the Langhe, drawn from vineyards in Monteu Roero, Santo Stefano Roero and Vezza d’Alba facing southwest and west. For 2023 the vines were 28 to 34 years old and yields were held to 45 hectolitres per hectare. The grapes fermented and macerated for 25 days in stainless steel, went through malolactic fermentation, and aged 14 months in French oak before bottling in January 2025. Giacosa describes violets and ripe blackberries, with a fine, well-structured palate: a younger, more approachable glimpse of the house style.
